grades.quote: A directory is implemented internally much like a file. Its inode has type T_DIR and its data is a sequence of directory entries. Each entry is a struct dirent (4165), which contains a name and an inode number.
grades.reason: The passage explains two of the three layers. An inode is the on-disk file object, and a directory is an inode of type T_DIR whose data is directory entries. Each entry maps a name to an inode number, so the entry is the naming layer that points to the inode. It also touches on dirlookup returning inodes. It never mentions file descriptors, so it can't complete the three-way comparison.
